newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - June 9.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - June 9.

text.p: Town mourns three brothers: The tiny south Taranaki township of Rahotu was in shock on Monday night after three brothers from the town were killed in a tow-car crash. Page 1.

Peters likely to insist on apology to caucus: NZ First leader Winston Peters is expected to make Te Tai Hauauru MP Tukoroirangi Morgan apologise at the party's caucus meeting tomorrow for misleading his leader over a failed attempt to sell an interview to a television channel. Page 1.

Employment Court role questioned: Finance Minister Bill Birch has questioned the need for a separate Employment Court to deal with labour market disputes, in light of criticsm over "judicial activism". Page 2.
Bank 'may be forced to act': The Reserve Bank could be forced to act if monetary conditions remain loose, according to the ANZ Bank. Page 11.
Chinese paper planned: A new Chinese-language morning newspaper with a cover price of $1 will hit the streets on Saturday, aiming at a New Zealand daily circulation of 3000 to 5000. Page 11.

Moves afoot to change measurement of housing costs in consumers price index: The Reserve Bank and the Treasury are pressing for a change in the way the cost of housing is reflected in the comsumers price index.
Sales of wine to US double: Sales of wine to the United States have more than doubled in value and volume this year.
North farmers seek meat marketing link: A joint-venture company directly linking New Zealand farmeres and overseas meat marketers should be set up, says Northland Federated Farmers.
Mainfreight cuts shipping times: Mainfreight International has introduced a time-saving trans-Tasman freight service to assist smaller exporters.

Captain thwarts twins' midnight bid to rejoin ship: The Canterbury twins, Joanne and Sarah Ingham, were spotted in the Port of Lyttelton trying to board the Malaysian container ship Bunga Terasek about 12.30am on Sunday, authorities said.
Timaru job cuts likely: Rationalisation plans announced by Alliance Textiles could result in job losses at the company's Timaru factory.
